# `07-pricing` — Pricing Engine

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tier** | T1 |
| **Status** | `in-progress` |

## Purpose

MarketState + configuration -> ClientQuote. Markup, spread policy, symbol configuration and tiering. A pure function, so it can be replayed and proven.

## Depends on

- [`06-market-data`](06-market-data.md) — Market Data
- [`01-domain-kernel`](01-domain-kernel.md) — Domain Kernel (types + math)

## Depended on by

- [`08-pnl-margin`](08-pnl-margin.md) — P&L and Margin
- [`19-client-api`](19-client-api.md) — Client API

## Inputs

- MarketState
- pricing configuration
- client tier

## Outputs

- ClientQuote

## What gets built

- pure pricing function (no I/O, no clock reads, no hidden state)
- markup / spread / tier configuration as versioned data
- stale-input and invalid-market rejection
- quote identity and quote expiry

## Invariants

These are executed as tests at gate **G4**. A module may not declare an
invariant it does not test.

- INV-060: identical (MarketState, config) input yields byte-identical ClientQuote output.
- INV-061: bid <= ask on every emitted quote, unless the model explicitly permits and labels a crossed state.
- INV-062: a quote derived from stale market state is never emitted as live.
- INV-063: every quote is attributable to the exact config version and market state that produced it.

## Test obligations

- determinism: same input, same output, across processes and machines
- property: bid <= ask; markup monotonicity
- rejection of stale, crossed and invalid inputs
- hot-path performance gate

## Known failure modes

The things that go wrong in systems like this one. Each should map to a test above.

- config hot-reload racing a quote computation
- clock read inside the pricing function breaking replay
